unsupervised-learning.name: Unsupervised Learning
unsupervised-learning.bio: Podcast: AI Vibe Check: Lab Wars, Why APIs Might Vanish & Future Predictions

html_en:
Open-weight AI may be entering its twilight, Anthropic quietly broke Claude Code and is now making amends, and the pressure on every professional role to reinvent itself keeps mounting — a full day's worth of structural shifts compressed into a Tuesday.

The Open-Weight Reckoning

The most consequential conversation happening in AI circles right now isn't about a flashy new model — it's about whether the era of freely available frontier weights is quietly coming to an end. On the Unsupervised Learning podcast, Rob from Radical Ventures laid out a thesis that's worth sitting with:

"My working assumption had been that the closed source proprietary models would advance the frontier... but the open frontier would only be a few months behind. I think there are signs now that near-frontier open weight AI [risks] falling off altogether. Meta, which historically has been the open weight champion in the West, is pulling back. And then the Chinese labs — whether it's Qwen or DeepSeek or others — their most high-performing models, they're now keeping proprietary behind an API."
— Rob, Radical Ventures, Unsupervised Learning

Co-panelist Ari (Datalogy, formerly DeepMind and Meta) largely agreed on the economics, if not the capability trajectory:

"The economic decision making around building and releasing open models has definitely changed... I am a lot more bearish on how many open models there will be going forward. It seemed like there was this cornucopia of open models that was only ever growing in 2025. The financial incentives just don't make sense — once you've achieved credibility, you want to start selling hosted inference and opening it up fully undermines your business."
— Ari, Unsupervised Learning

Which makes the timing of Guillermo Rauch's surprise endorsement this week particularly interesting. The Vercel CEO posted that he was "genuinely impressed, almost shocked, at how good GLM-5.2 by @zai_org is at coding. This changes things." — a rare piece of unqualified enthusiasm from someone who sees a lot of models. Box CEO Aaron Levie offered the counterpoint worth remembering: even if open weights narrow the gap on specific tasks, frontier models still win on orchestration, planning, and review — and cheaper open models ultimately expand the total market for everyone. Watch/Listen: AI Vibe Check: Lab Wars, Why APIs Might Vanish & Future Predictions

Anthropic's Honest Post-Mortem

Anthropic published a remarkably candid post-mortem on why Claude Code felt noticeably worse over the past month — and the explanation is less "model degradation" and more "three separate self-inflicted wounds." The short version: they silently reduced reasoning effort from high to medium to cut latency, a caching bug made Claude forget its own prior reasoning mid-session, and an overzealous verbosity-reduction prompt hurt code quality. Each change hit different users on different schedules, making the aggregate look like mysterious, inconsistent degradation.

All three have been reverted as of April 20. Users are getting usage limits reset as a goodwill gesture. The piece is worth reading in full — not because the mistakes are unusual, but because the transparency about how hard it is to catch quality regressions in production is genuinely instructive. As they note, "neither our internal usage nor evals initially reproduced the issues identified."

Meanwhile, Anthropic also published a deeper engineering piece on Managed Agents — their hosted service for long-running agentic tasks — explaining the architectural decision to decouple Claude's "brain" from its "hands." The analogy to operating system design is apt: just as read() works whether you're on a 1970s disk pack or a modern SSD, the goal is interfaces that outlast any particular implementation. And today they announced self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels in beta, letting enterprise customers keep agent execution entirely within their own security perimeter.

An OpenAI engineer, @thsottiaux, offered a teaser from the competition's side that landed with 3,000+ likes:

"We built the Codex App with models that were okayish at front-end. Wait to see what we can do when we finally improve front-end capabilities significantly in our models. That day will be something."

Engineers as Managers, PMs as Builders

The agentic shift isn't just a product story — it's quietly reorganizing entire job descriptions. The Unsupervised Learning crew captured the engineering side well:

"We're really starting to see the shift of engineers almost all moving from ICs to managers of agents... More and more people are now context-switching between managing different agents rather than just kind of working on the one thing."
— Ari, Unsupervised Learning

Though the same researchers noted the hidden costs: "It's a lot easier to produce a massive amount of code that can do something. But now you have this pretty massive understanding gap... The bottlenecks just seem to shift."

On the product side, @realmadhuguru made a sharp distinction between the PM who uses AI to produce more of the same artifacts — "more PRDs, more strategy decks, more docs" — and what they're calling the Builder PM: someone who runs agents for research, queries logs directly, generates competing prototypes, and ships demos instead of documents. "Engineers react far more constructively to demos than docs," they note — which sounds obvious, but the organizational inertia around documents-as-output runs deep.

Peter Yang offered a grounding data point from the other side of the hype: he can barely use up his $200/month Codex and Claude subscriptions, and doesn't see the point of running local models when hosted inference is already more than sufficient for his workload. It's a useful reminder that the "frontier at all costs" mentality isn't universal.

Keeping Your Mental Model Fresh

Nikunj put plainly what many practitioners feel but rarely articulate:

"The biggest problem with AI is that priors need to be reset every few weeks... I talk to so many people who say xyz doesn't work and when I ask when was the last time they tried testing it, the answer is always 'a few months ago.' Brother that's like eons ago in AI timelines. Each person needs to have their own evals of hard tasks and weekly tinker time to truly understand where the frontier is. And then you need to talk to enterprise buyers weekly who are usually two years behind. The combination of the two will give you a pretty good sense of where to invest time and capital."

And finally, Amjad Masad of Replit offered the most poetic framing of the week — a reminder of just how strange this moment actually is:

"We posted for twenty years, thinking we were talking to each other. Then the transformer came online, and the network read what we'd written, and became itself."
html_zh:
开源模型的黄金时代或许正在落幕，而 Anthropic 则在大力构建企业级 Agent 基础设施——今天的 AI 圈，两条叙事线索同时收紧。

🔓 开源模型的转折点：免费午餐要结束了？

本周最引人深思的讨论，围绕开源权重模型的未来展开。Guillermo Rauch 率先点燃话题，对智谱最新发布的 GLM-5.2 赞不绝口：

对 @zai_org 的 GLM-5.2 在编程方面的表现感到真正的震惊。这改变了很多事情。

但 Aaron Levie 的观察更具战略眼光——他认为开源模型与前沿模型之间的差距正在收窄，这对整个应用层是好消息：

开源权重模型越能维持与前沿的微小差距，而不是差距越来越大，AI 能创造的价值就越多……这对 AI 应用层来说非常有利，现在可以用更便宜的模型来优化成本。

然而，Unsupervised Learning 播客中，来自 Radical 的 Rob 泼了一盆冷水。Watch/Listen: AI Vibe Check: Lab Wars, Why APIs Might Vanish & Future Predictions

Meta 历来是西方开源的旗手，但似乎正在撤退，不太可能延续其开源策略。中国实验室则在把最高性能的模型锁在 API 背后，只开源性能较弱的小模型……如果你想要真正的前沿人工智能，你必须向一家公司付费购买专有模型。

Datalogy 的 Ari 补充道，这不是能力趋势的变化，而是经济激励的逆转：

我们可能已经达到了开放模型数量的峰值，接下来只会越来越少。一旦你建立了信誉，就会想要开始销售托管推理服务，完全开放模型会直接破坏你的商业模式。

讽刺的是，就在这场讨论进行的同时，Peter Yang 直言不讳地代表了许多实际用户的感受：

我的 Codex 和 Claude $200 订阅都用不完，所以我实在看不出跑本地模型的意义……要在本地运行最新的 GLM 需要 512MB 显存，那得是一台价值一万美元的 Mac Studio？

🤖 Anthropic 的企业 Agent 大棋：把大脑和手分开

Anthropic 本周发布了一系列重要的工程博客和产品更新，核心主题只有一个：让企业级 Agent 既能跑得远，又能跑得安全。

在 Managed Agents 架构博客中，Anthropic 工程团队描述了他们解决"宠物与牲口"难题的方式——把 Agent 的"大脑"（Claude 和其调度器）与"双手"（沙箱和工具）彻底解耦：

我们把 Agent 的各个组件虚拟化：一个 session（所有事件的只读日志）、一个 harness（调用 Claude 并路由工具调用的循环）以及一个 sandbox（Claude 可以运行代码和编辑文件的执行环境）。这样每个组件的实现都可以自由替换，而不影响其他部分。

更实际的企业落地则体现在同日发布的 自托管沙箱与 MCP 隧道功能上。Agent 的执行环境可以运行在企业自己的基础设施内，敏感数据不再需要离开企业边界，同时还能通过加密隧道连接内部私有网络中的 MCP 服务器。Cloudflare、Daytona、Modal、Vercel 均已成为支持的沙箱提供商。

🐛 当 Claude Code 开始"变笨"：一次罕见的公开复盘

Anthropic 还发布了一篇颇为难得的事后复盘文章，坦承过去数月 Claude Code 质量下降的根本原因。文章揭示了三个独立的工程失误叠加，造成了看似"广泛、不一致的退步"：推理强度被悄悄从 high 降为 medium、一个缓存优化 bug 让 Claude 在同一会话中反复"失忆"、以及一条降低冗长度的系统提示指令损害了代码质量。

我们从不故意降低模型质量，并立即确认 API 和推理层未受影响……由于每次变更影响的是不同的流量切片，叠加效果看起来像是广泛、不一致的退步。

Anthropic 表示，截至 4 月 23 日，已为所有订阅用户重置使用限制，并将 Opus 4.7 的默认推理强度提升至 xhigh。这篇复盘的价值不只在于解释了"发生了什么"，更在于它明确承认：即便是内部 eval 也未能在早期复现问题——这对整个行业如何设计质量监控体系，是一个值得深思的教训。

👔 PM 角色的自我革命：文档已死，原型当道

当工程师们纷纷从 IC 转型为"Agent 管理者"，产品经理的角色也在悄然撕裂。@realmadhuguru 的一条推文引发广泛共鸣，他将 PM 分为两类：

老派 PM 用 AI 加速原有工作：更多 PRD、更多战略文档……Builder PM 则用 AI 扩展自己在产品全生命周期中的角色……他们的输出越来越多是原型而非文档——工程师对 Demo 的反应远比对文档积极得多。

这与 Unsupervised Learning 播客中对工程师角色转变的观察形成了呼应。编码 Agent 开始在更长时间维度上真正"跑起来"，但随之而来的是新的瓶颈：

现在产生大量代码容易多了，但随之而来的是巨大的理解鸿沟，也更容易把技术债塞进代码库……瓶颈只是转移了，而不是消失了。

最后，Replit 创始人 Amjad Masad 用一句诗意的话，为这个时代做了注脚：

我们发帖二十年，以为是在彼此交谈。然后 Transformer 上线了，网络读完了我们写的一切，并由此成为了它自己。
